proposals.before: Jing's troops were Qiang and Hu of mixed stock; they jostled those on either side with great insolence. The guards did not flinch or yield—only Buhai and palace attendant Xu Chi stood unmoved at the emperor's side.
proposals.after: Jing's troops were Qiang and Hu of mixed stock; they jostled those on either side with great insolence. The guards were startled and gave way—only Buhai and palace attendant Xu Chi stood unmoved at the emperor's side.
proposals.reason: Chinese 侍衛者不驚恐辟易 contrasted with 唯…不動 requires the guards to yield; the English negation contradicts the following “only”.

proposals.before: Jing's soldiers were all mixed breeds of Qiang and Hu; they charged left and right, very insolent. The guards did not startle or give way—only Buhai and palace attendant Xu Chi stood at the side unmoved.
proposals.after: Jing's soldiers were all mixed breeds of Qiang and Hu; they charged left and right, very insolent. The guards were startled and gave way—only Buhai and palace attendant Xu Chi stood at the side unmoved.
proposals.reason: Same contradiction as the idiomatic line: only Buhai and Xu Chi remained unmoved.

proposals.before: At the time, emperor Jianwen was confined by Jing, he sent someone to request that Buhai dwell with him; Jing assented, and Buhai waited on him with ever greater care.
proposals.after: When Emperor Jianwen was confined by Jing, he sent someone to request that Buhai dwell with him; Jing assented, and Buhai waited on him with ever greater care.
proposals.reason: “At the time,” misrenders 及 and leaves a comma splice; literal correctly uses “When”.

proposals.before: At the time, emperor Yuan of Liang took the throne, he made Buhai a Secretariat gentleman and concurrently director of the Court Tribunal, and thus led his household west.
proposals.after: When Emperor Yuan of Liang took the throne, he made Buhai a Secretariat gentleman and concurrently director of the Court Tribunal, and thus led his household west.
proposals.reason: “At the time,” misrenders 及/when-clause and creates a comma splice; literal is correct.

proposals.before: Houzhu thereupon ordered attendant Wenqing Shi [2], "Xie Zhen at the prince's establishment has no salary or rank; grant him one hundred piculs of grain."
proposals.after: Houzhu thereupon ordered attendant Shi Wenqing [2], "Xie Zhen at the prince's establishment has no salary or rank; grant him one hundred piculs of grain."
proposals.reason: Chinese 施文慶 is Shi Wenqing; English reversed the surname/personal name order.

proposals.before: Houzhu thereupon ordered the attendant Wenqing Shi, [to say]: "Xie Zhen at the prince's establishment has no salary or rank; one hundred piculs of grain may be granted."
proposals.after: Houzhu thereupon ordered the attendant Shi Wenqing, [to say]: "Xie Zhen at the prince's establishment has no salary or rank; one hundred piculs of grain may be granted."
proposals.reason: Same surname/personal-name reversal as the idiomatic line.

proposals.before: When mourning ended, as a kinsman by marriage and a younger clansman he was admitted to audience; Emperor Wu of Liang saw Hao emaciated, sighed a long while, and said to father and son Zichan:
proposals.after: When mourning ended, as a kinsman by marriage and a younger clansman he was admitted to audience; Emperor Wu of Liang saw Hao emaciated, sighed a long while, and said to his father Zichan:
proposals.reason: 其父子產 means “his father Zichan”, not “father and son Zichan”.

decisions.reason: Chapter s0022 lacks 莫 (侍衛者不驚恐辟易), but 唯不害…侍側不動 requires that the other guards did yield; critical editions restore 莫不驚恐辟易, and the proposed idiomatic correctly renders that sense.
Same unit: the chapter’s 不 without 莫 is corrupt against 唯…不動; editions reading 莫不驚恐辟易 support “were startled and gave way” in the literal.
及簡文為景所幽 is a temporal “when” clause, not discourse “At the time,”; the original also leaves a comma splice, and the proposed wording matches the Chinese and the already-correct literal.

梁元帝立 is a circumstantial “when he took the throne” clause; “At the time,” is unsupported padding and creates a comma splice, while the proposed “When Emperor Yuan…” matches the Chinese and the literal.
施文慶 is surname 施 (Shi) plus given name 文慶 (Wenqing); “Wenqing Shi” reverses Chinese name order, and the proposed Shi Wenqing restores it.
Same name order error in the literal: 施文慶 must be Shi Wenqing, not Wenqing Shi.
其父子產 means “his father Zichan” (父 + name 子產), as already in s0122; “father and son Zichan” invents a father–son pair.
